annotation.method: Codex read the complete local paper, surveyed its inversion, QR, LU, rank-revealing, Schur, singular-value, Sylvester, and eigenvector claims, rejected delegated, asymptotic-only, complexity-only, sketch-only, and redundant candidates, searched the frozen mathlib and mounted NumStability object baselines, visually checked every selected source page, and compiled private N/L proofs before accepting the targets.
annotation.reason: The project owner assigned the P10 source selection and benchmark annotation to Codex.

corpus_membership: This paper is part of the current corpus listed in metadata/manifest.json.
paper_version: published journal version; volume 108, 2007, printed pages 59-91

rejected_candidates.candidate: the matrix-multiplication stability model (1) and the general logarithmic-stability conclusions
rejected_candidates.reason: Equation (1) is an assumed interface inherited from prior work, while the headline conclusions are asymptotic complexity and stability claims rather than compact exact finite targets.
The theorem is a bit-complexity conversion whose proof depends on asymptotic O notation, condition-number growth, and a precision-cost model; it is not a concise finite numerical bound.

rejected_candidates.candidate: the recursive triangular and dense matrix-inversion conclusions after equation (8)
rejected_candidates.reason: Their displayed solutions are asymptotic and invoke an external recurrence theorem. T1 and T2 instead preserve equation (8)'s exact reusable error-propagation content.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Lemma 4.1 on recursive QR and Lemma 4.2 on LU decomposition
rejected_candidates.reason: Both are broad algorithmic backward-stability results with O(epsilon) statements and substantial block-algorithm models; the LU result also carries structural assumptions not suitable for a compact condition-neutral target.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Lemma 5.1, Theorem 5.2, and Lemma 5.4 on randomized rank-revealing decompositions
rejected_candidates.reason: The candidates mix probabilistic or generic matrix choices, singular-value perturbation machinery, and O(epsilon) claims; a literal task would require a much larger random-matrix and decomposition model.

rejected_candidates.candidate: the rank-revealing, Schur, and singular-value decomposition reductions in Sections 5-6
rejected_candidates.reason: Several stability conclusions are delegated to earlier references or given as high-level algorithm reductions and asymptotic recurrences rather than self-contained finite estimates.

rejected_candidates.candidate: the generalized Sylvester extension after equation (20)
rejected_candidates.reason: The paper explicitly says the analogous approach is only sketched; the ordinary Sylvester recurrence is fully displayed and supplies the more faithful finite target.

rejected_candidates.candidate: equation (21) and the recursive eigenvector algorithm
rejected_candidates.reason: Equation (21) is a block factorization used to define an algorithm, while the subsequent accuracy discussion is conditional, asymptotic, and not presented as an exact finite theorem.

T1.decision: Use the inherited-right-input Frobenius product estimate appearing as one term of equation (8); the frozen library supplies it directly.

T2.decision: Use an exact finite completion of equation (8), combining local, inherited-left, inherited-right, and explicit cross-term budgets.

T3.decision: Use a new exact finite unrolling of the recursive Sylvester error recurrence whose asymptotic solution is equation (20).

selection_policy: Use exact finite claims made or algebraically completed from displayed arguments in this paper.
Reject definitions, experiments, complexity-only statements, delegated results, sketches, and claims whose literal content is vague asymptotics.
Expose the second-order inherited-error product explicitly when exactifying the first-order product rule.
Keep the fixed Lean setting condition-neutral and paper-scoped.
Assign tiers only after checking the mounted frozen object baseline, not merely the broader source tree.
